sections.title: Habit and identification
sections.text: The catalogue entry Carpinus refers here to Carpinus betulus, European hornbeam, a deciduous tree native from temperate Europe into western Asia. It usually reaches 20–25 m. Its doubly toothed leaves are about 8–10 cm long and often remain on the branches after drying.

sections.title: Catkins and fruit
sections.text: Male catkins reach about 6 cm and female catkins may reach 15 cm. Each small nutlet is associated with a three-lobed bract about 3.5 cm long; the plate correctly shows this leafy bract, which is not a wing of the fruit. No common food use is established.

sources.title: Carpinus betulus — European Atlas of Forest Tree Species, European Commission
